arxiv-2006-12099.creator: Wangmei Zha, James Daniel Brandenburg, Lijuan Ruan, Zebo Tang, Zhangbu Xu
arxiv-2006-12099.description: Abstract The linearly polarized quasi-real photons from the highly Lorentz-contracted Coulomb fields of relativistic heavy ions can fluctuate to quark-antiquark pairs, scatter off a target nucleus and emerge as vector mesons. In the process, the two colliding nuclei can switch roles to act as photon emitter or target, forming a double-slit interference pattern.

arxiv-2301-03556.title: Impact of nuclear shape fluctuations in high-energy heavy ion collisions
arxiv-2301-03556.creator: Aman Dimri, Somadutta Bhatta, Jiangyong Jia
arxiv-2301-03556.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Aman Dimri, Somadutta Bhatta, Jiangyong Jia. We investigate the impact of nuclear shape fluctuations on the initial state geometry in heavy ion collisions, particularly its eccentricity ε 2 \varepsilon_{2} and inverse size d ⟂ d_{\perp} , which can be related to the elliptic and radial flow in the final state.

arxiv-2408-12444.creator: Aydin Abadi
arxiv-2408-12444.description: Abstract Time-Lock Puzzles (TLPs) have been developed to securely transmit sensitive information into the future without relying on a trusted third party. Multi-instance TLP is a scalable variant of TLP that enables a server to efficiently find solutions to different puzzles provided by a client at once. Nevertheless, existing multi-instance TLPs lack support for (verifiable) homomorphic computation .

arxiv-2504-07780.title: Interference-caged quantum many-body scars: the Fock space topological localization and interference zeros
arxiv-2504-07780.creator: Tao-Lin Tan, Yi-Ping Huang
arxiv-2504-07780.description: Abstract We propose a general mechanism for realizing athermal finite-energy-density eigenstates—termed interference-caged quantum many-body scars (ICQMBS)—which originate from exact many-body destructive interference on the Fock space graph. These eigenstates are strictly localized to specific subsets of vertices, analogous to compact localized states in flat-band systems.
